mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: BVI Registry of Corporate Affairs (Registrar of Corporate Affairs, BVI Financial Services Commission)

ubo_and_aml_profiling.pep_and_sanctions_screening_protocols: Mandatory screening of all directors, shareholders holding 25% or more, ultimate beneficial owners, and authorized signatories against (i) the BVI Financial Services Commission sanctions notices; (ii) the UK Office of Financial Sanctions Implementation (OFSI) consolidated list; (iii) the United Nations Security Council consolidated sanctions list; (iv) the US OFAC SDN list (mandatory where USD Swift/Wire payment rails are used); and (v) BVI territorial sanctions orders under the UK Sanctions and Anti-Money Laundering Act 2018. Enhanced Due Diligence with 100-point identity verification and documented source-of-funds and source-of-wealth evidence is compulsory for PEPs, their family members, and close associates under the BVI AML/CFT Code of Practice. The medium-risk rating assigned to this pure equity holding SPV requires periodic AML file review at intervals no longer than 12 months.

statutory_name_clearance_protocol.registry_portal_name: BVI Registry of Corporate Affairs online e-registry portal (Registry of Corporate Affairs, BVI Financial Services Commission)
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.language_and_transliteration_doctrine: English is the exclusive statutory filing language. Names must be expressed in Latin-script characters; any foreign-language name is admissible only in Roman-alphabet transliteration and must be readily pronounceable and non-misleading. Each BVI Business Company name must end with a recognized corporate suffix: 'Limited', 'Ltd', 'Corporation', 'Incorporated', 'Inc', 'Societe Anonyme', or an approved abbreviation. The name must not be identical or deceptively similar to any name already registered, reserved, or recorded as a trademark in the BVI.
prohibited_and_sensitive_tokens: Institute (where implying a professional regulatory body)
British Virgin Islands (use restricted to government-designated entities)
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.extension_and_rejection_appeal_sop: Within 14 days of issuance of a name-rejection notice, the applicant must file a written administrative representation with the Registrar of Corporate Affairs stating the legal and factual grounds for reversal; the Registrar must issue a final decision within 21 days of receipt. If the refusal is upheld, the applicant may file an originating application with the BVI High Court of the Eastern Caribbean Supreme Court (BVI Civil Division) under the BVI Business Companies Act seeking an order directing registration, and in parallel may submit two or three alternative names in the same application cycle. Any reservation that would otherwise lapse during the appeal is extended administratively by the Registry until final determination.

registered_office_and_commercial_substan.virtual_office_permissibility: Not permissible for the statutory registered office. The BVI Business Companies Act, 2004 requires every Business Company to maintain a registered office physically located in the BVI, provided by a licensed corporate services provider (registered agent). A remote or virtual office address outside the BVI cannot satisfy this obligation. For a pure equity holding SPV, no separate physical premises, employees, or operational assets are required; the registered agent's physical BVI office fulfils the statutory mandate and, together with proper statutory records, satisfies the reduced economic substance expectations applicable to a pure equity holding business under the BVI Economic Substance (Companies and Limited Partnerships) Act, 2018.
registered_office_and_commercial_substan.physical_inspection_likelihood: Low (approximately 2% annual probability). The BVI Financial Services Commission historically prioritises unannounced on-site inspections of licensed financial institutions (trust companies, fund managers, banks, and insurance brokers). An unlicensed, passive, pure equity holding SPV is not a routine inspection target; an unannounced physical visit would realistically occur only upon a specific AML/CFT intelligence alert, a compliance complaint, or persistent failure to submit annual returns and economic substance declarations.

incorporation_legal_framework.governing_statute_and_sections: BVI Business Companies Act, 2004 (as amended), particularly sections 5 (incorporation), 9 (memorandum and articles), 17 (registered office), 27 (directors), 28 (register of directors) and 101 (register of members).
incorporation_legal_framework.competent_registry_authority: Registry of Corporate Affairs, Financial Services Commission of the British Virgin Islands (applications must be submitted through a licensed BVI registered agent).
incorporation_legal_framework.statutory_filing_instrument: Memorandum and Articles of Association accompanied by Form 1 (Notice of Registered Office and Registered Agent) filed via the BVI e-Registry system.
incorporation_legal_framework.minimum_paid_up_capital_rule: No minimum issued or paid-up capital. The Company may be incorporated with a single subscriber share of no par value and no paid-up capital; no escrow or capital deposit obligation applies.
incorporation_legal_framework.pro_forma_first_board_resolution_en:
RESOLVED that the incorporation of the Company under the BVI Business Companies Act, 2004 be and is hereby ratified and confirmed.

RESOLVED FURTHER that the subscription of one Ordinary Share of no par value by the initial subscriber be accepted, and that the subscriber be allotted one Ordinary Share in the Company's register of members.

RESOLVED FURTHER that the registered office of the Company be fixed at the office of [Registered Agent], Road Town, Tortola, British Virgin Islands.

RESOLVED FURTHER that [Director Name] be and is hereby appointed as the sole director, and [Officer Name] as secretary, each to serve until replaced and to exercise the authority conferred under the Company's Memorandum and Articles of Association.

step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: BVI Registry of Corporate Affairs (via licensed registered agent)
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Instruct a licensed BVI registered agent to search the company name index and reserve the preferred name. The agent submits a name reservation request through the BVI e-Registry, paying the applicable government fee. The reservation is valid for 60 days. Confirm no prohibited or identical name exists before filing incorporation documents. No notarization is required for the reservation.
required_dossiers: Client instruction letter confirming preferred company name
Identification proof of beneficial owner for agent's anti-money-laundering file
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the name is rejected because it is similar to an existing company or contains a prohibited word, the agent will promptly submit alternative names from a shortlist and reserve the next available option; the reservation fee is non-refundable.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Preparation and Filing of Incorporation Application
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: BVI Registry of Corporate Affairs (via licensed registered agent)
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: The registered agent prepares the Memorandum and Articles of Association (M&A) and the initial notice of registered office and registered agent (Form 1) in accordance with the BVI Business Companies Act. The subscriber signs the M&A. The agent then files the M&A, Form 1, and director appointment information together with the certified corporate application via the e-Registry system. The government incorporation fee is paid.
required_dossiers: Signed Memorandum and Articles of Association
Form 1 - Notice of Registered Office and Registered Agent
Proof of identity and residential address of each subscriber
Copy of the registered agent's consent to act
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the Registry queries the application (e.g., incomplete financial information or name conflict), the agent will submit a written response and any corrected forms within the specified deadline; a resubmission may attract an additional fee if not resolved at first query.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Issue of Certificate of Incorporation and Statutory Registers
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Upon successful review, the Registry issues a Certificate of Incorporation with the company number and date. The registered agent obtains the certificate and prepares the statutory registers: register of members, register of directors, and register of charges. The company becomes a separate legal person from the date stated in the certificate. A brief filing acknowledgement is retained.
required_dossiers: Certificate of Incorporation issued by the Registry
Statutory register template completed by the registered agent
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the certificate is delayed due to a Registry error, the agent may apply for expedited processing and request a written status update; any typographical error in the certificate will be corrected by filing a formal request for amendment.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Registered Office and Registered Agent Appointment Confirmation
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: BVI Financial Services Commission / Registered Agent
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: The registered office must be located in the British Virgin Islands at the address of the licensed registered agent. The agent will ensure the Form 1 is correctly registered and the registered office is accessible during normal business hours. The company's registered agent maintains the legal presence for service of process and regulatory correspondence.
required_dossiers: Consent to act as registered agent
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the registered agent resigns, the company must appoint a new agent and file a new Form 1 within 21 days; failure to do so may result in striking-off, so a standby agent should be pre-designated.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Convening First Board Meeting and Officer Appointments
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: The initial director convenes the first board meeting (virtual or physical). A written resolution is adopted confirming the allotment of shares, fixing the registered office, and appointing officers (director, secretary, and such other persons as may be required). The resolution is signed by the director and retained in the company's minute book. Officer consents are obtained and the register of directors updated.
required_dossiers: First board resolution signed by the initial director
Consent to act from each appointed officer
Register of Directors and Officers update
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If an officer appointment is invalid or a consent is withdrawn, a new resolution appointing a substitute officer should be passed and filed in company records; if the director fails to act, the sole member may call an extraordinary meeting.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.competent_industrial_authority: Not applicable – the entity is a pure equity-holding SPV with no industrial activity in the United Kingdom or the British Virgin Islands.
industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.operating_license_title: No industrial operating license required under BVI or UK law for passive holding of shares.

environmental_impact_assessment_eia.agency_name: Not applicable – no EIA competent agency filing for a non-operating holding vehicle.
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.classification_tier: Exempt – no physical development, construction, or operational activity.
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.discharge_and_emissions_standards: No wastewater, VOC, or waste streams arise; therefore no emission limits apply.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.civil_defense_and_occupational_clearance: Not applicable – no employees, premises, or workplace. Fire safety certification, structural inspections, and occupational clearance are not triggered.

national_tax_registration_infrastructure.competent_tax_authority: Her Majesty's Revenue and Customs (HMRC); online portal via GOV.UK Government Gateway (www.gov.uk/hmrc) and HMRC Developer Hub for Making Tax Digital (MTD) APIs.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.tax_id_procurement_sop: Step 1: Determine UK tax residence — a BVI Business Company (opaque body corporate) is UK-resident only if central management and control is exercised in the UK; if so, register for UK Corporation Tax via HMRC Form CT41G within 3 months of commencing activity to obtain a 10-digit Unique Taxpayer Reference (UTR). Step 2: If non-UK resident, register for Corporation Tax (Form CT41G 'Non-Resident Company' version) only where it carries on a UK trade through a permanent establishment (PE) or derives UK-source income chargeable to UK tax. Step 3: For a pure, passive equity holding SPV that makes no taxable supplies and has no UK PE, no mandatory UK tax registration arises; the entity relies on BVI tax-exempt status (BVI levies 0% tax on offshore passive income). Step 4: If the SPV later makes UK taxable supplies (e.g., management charges), apply for VAT registration online via GOV.UK (Form VAT1/VAT1B; non-UK established persons have no annual threshold and must register before making any UK taxable supply). Step 5: Obtain a UK EORI number via HMRC's online application for any customs declarations or import/export activity. Step 6: Appoint a UK tax representative if HMRC requires one for non-resident registrations.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.default_entity_tax_classification: Tax_Exempt_Zone — the BVI BC is treated by the UK as an opaque, entity-level taxed company (no US-style pass-through eligibility); it is outside UK Corporation Tax unless UK resident (central management and control test) or trading through a UK PE. As a BVI-domiciled entity, it enjoys 0% BVI corporate tax on worldwide passive income; dividends and capital gains from qualifying shareholdings are generally exempt from UK tax under CTA 2009 Part 9A (dividend exemption) and CTA 2010 Schedule 7AC (Substantial Shareholding Exemption), provided UK tax residence and UK PE status are avoided.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.statutory_election_mechanisms: The UK has no check-the-box entity classification election; legal form under foreign law governs opacity. Available elections: (1) Hybrid mismatch designated election under CTA 2010 s.259CB to treat a tax-transparent entity as an opaque company where the SPV holds interests in transparent vehicles; (2) CFC holding-company exemption and excluded-territories election under TIOPA 2010 Part 9A to relieve passive equity income from the UK Controlled Foreign Company charge; (3) Substantial Shareholding Exemption pooling election under CTA 2009 Schedule 7AC to preserve continuity of shareholding across the group; (4) VAT group registration election under VATA 1994 s.43 to treat the BVI SPV and its UK subsidiaries as a single taxable person for UK VAT; (5) Option to tax (election to waive exemption) under VATA 1994 Schedule 10 only if UK real estate is subsequently acquired — not applicable to a pure equity holding SPV.

indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.indirect_tax_system_name: UK Value Added Tax (VAT) — governed by the Value Added Tax Act 1994 and HMRC VAT Notices; independent UK VAT regime post-Brexit, aligned to OECD standards but no longer subject to the EU VAT Directive.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.statutory_registration_threshold_local_c: £90,000 annual taxable turnover threshold for UK-established businesses (effective 1 April 2024); non-UK established persons (including the BVI BC) have NO registration threshold and must register from the first taxable supply made in the UK; pure dividend income and share-disposal proceeds are outside the scope of UK VAT (not consideration for a supply), so no VAT registration is triggered by the SPV's passive holding activities.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.electronic_invoicing_and_clearance_manda: No real-time fiscal clearance mandate, no digital stamping regime, and no mandatory B2B e-invoicing clearance gateway in the UK. Mandatory 'Making Tax Digital for VAT' (MTD) applies to all VAT-registered businesses: digital record-keeping and quarterly submission of VAT returns to HMRC via Functional Compatible Software using HMRC Application Programming Interfaces (APIs). B2B e-invoicing is voluntary; PEPPOL BIS 3.0, EDI and PDF formats are accepted where the customer agrees. HMRC operates risk-based analytics and MTD fraud detection rather than a central invoice pre-clearance system.

export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.zero_rating_eligibility: Zero rating applies to: (1) export of goods — the supply involves removal of goods from the UK to a destination outside the UK within 3 months of the time of supply (or longer where HMRC allows), with the exporter retaining valid commercial and customs evidence of physical export (VATA 1994 s.30 and Schedule 4 paragraph 6; HMRC Notice 703); (2) international B2B services — services supplied to a business customer outside the UK are outside the scope of UK VAT under place-of-supply rules (VATA 1994 Schedule 4A; SI 1992/3121), with reverse charge applying to the customer; (3) for the BVI BC pure equity SPV — dividend receipts and share disposal proceeds are outside the VAT net entirely (no supply), so no VAT charge arises and no input VAT recovery is available on costs attributable to exempt or outside-scope activities unless a partial exemption method or option to tax is later adopted.
mandatory_customs_documentation_bundle: Customs Export Declaration (CDS/SAD Form C88) evidencing release of goods from the UK customs territory
Bill of Lading, Air Waybill, CMR consignment note, or postal/courier receipt proving physical export within the statutory time limit

Inward Remittance Certificate or bank FX credit advice evidencing receipt of export consideration (required where HMRC challenges valuation or FX repatriation in high-risk audits, though not a general UK statutory condition)
Commercial invoice and underlying export sales contract
Packing list or export cargo report
Forwarder's certificate of shipment where a freight forwarder arranges export
export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.audit_scrutiny_and_clawback_penalties: HMRC may assess and claw back zero-rated output tax where export evidence is incomplete, goods did not leave the UK, or the transaction is found to be artificial (VATA 1994 s.73; assessment window of 4 years for careless conduct and 20 years for deliberate concealment or offshore-related matters). Civil penalties apply under FA 2007 Schedule 24: up to 30% of Potential Lost Revenue for careless errors, 70% for deliberate errors, and 100% for deliberate and concealed errors, plus default interest under VATA 1994 s.74; failure-to-notify penalties may reach 100% of the tax. Fraudulent export zero-rating (e.g., Missing Trader Intra-Community-style diversion fraud, forged Bills of Lading, or false customs declarations) is a criminal offence under VATA 1994 s.72 and CEMA 1979, carrying imprisonment of up to 7 years, unlimited fines, and director personal liability; HMRC may also issue joint and several liability notices under VATA 1994 s.77A (goods) and s.77B (services) to parties who knew or had reasonable grounds to suspect VAT fraud.

fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.central_bank_authority: Bank of England (UK central bank and Prudential Regulation Authority); HM Treasury (financial sanctions and sovereign-level economic policy); HM Revenue & Customs (tax and disclosure); United Kingdom has no dedicated foreign exchange administration and no central-planning FX control authority.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.currency_convertibility_assessment: The UK maintains full current-account and capital-account convertibility under Article VIII of the IMF Articles of Agreement. There are no UK exchange controls requiring central-bank approval for equity subscription, dividend remittance, or loan repayments. Profit remittance from a UK-resident subsidiary to a BVI Business Company is restricted only by the Companies Act 2006 solvency/distribution test and, where applicable, UK withholding tax on interest/royalties and the UK dividends tax regime for exempt or treaty-protected recipients. Sanctions screening, anti-money-laundering verification, and CRS/FATCA reporting are compliance filters, not currency controls.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.export_proceeds_surrender_rules: The UK imposes no statutory surrender, repatriation timeline, or mandatory conversion ratio for export receipts. Export proceeds may be held in any currency or bank account, subject to HMRC record-keeping, transfer-pricing documentation, sanctions/AML checks, and, for the BVI holding entity, the tax-residence analysis under UK common-law central management and control. This position also applies to non-resident BVI pure-equity holding SPVs that merely hold UK or EU operating subsidiaries.

tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.account_class: Multi-currency Operational Account / Capital Escrow Account

corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.fintech_emi_cross_border_viability: Feasibility rating: Medium. UK-authorised e-money institutions (EMIs) regulated by the Financial Conduct Authority under the Electronic Money Regulations 2011 and the MLRs 2017 may onboard a BVI Business Company remotely, but legal constraints and commercial appetite vary materially. The BVI BC is not prohibited from holding an EMI account; however, many EMIs decline pure holding SPVs with no UK operational substance, especially when the UBO and directors are non-resident, because the business model increases unexplained-transaction risk. A fully digitised EDD file, including certificate of incorporation, good standing certificate, register of directors and members, registered-agent compliance letter, economic-substance explanation, and source-of-wealth dossier, is required. Unregulated offshore digital EMIs are not permitted to hold out as UK-licensed institutions and are not recommended for regulated treasury flows.
corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.physical_presence_and_kyc_interview_mand: No UK statute requires directors to appear physically at a UK bank branch for all corporate onboarding, and the MLRs 2017 expressly contemplate risk-based remote customer due diligence. However, risk-based onboarding practice is bifurcated: tier-1 UK banks generally allow a recorded video interview with the directors plus notarised certified passport copies and rely on the BVI registered agent's corporate pack; absent an existing banking relationship, a London branch interview or an introducer attendance by a UK-regulated solicitor/accountant may be imposed. A BVI company that has no UBO with prior UK banking history should expect enhanced due diligence, possible personal appearance of the majority director, and physical verification of registered-office documentation.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: BVI company with only a registered agent address and no local economic substance
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Certificate of incorporation, certificate of good standing from the BVI Registry/FSC, memorandum and articles of association, certificate of incumbency, current register of directors and members, BVI registered-agent corporate-compliance letter, group organisational chart, statement that the entity is a pure-equity holding SPV excluded from substantive economic-substance requirements, and, if managed outside the UK, a tax-residence analysis confirming no UK central management and control.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Nominee directors or nominee shareholders causing uncertainty over beneficial ownership
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Executed declarations of directorship/shareholding, clear UBO cascade to natural person(s) at 25% or more, trust or foundation constitutional documents if relevant, powers of attorney, professional indemnity confirmations from the BVI corporate services provider, and a written explanation for each nominee arrangement with corroborating commercial rationale.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Source of funds or source of wealth derived from cross-border equity subscription with insufficient transaction trail
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Monthly bank statements for the preceding 12-24 months, audited financial statements of the ultimate parent or shareholder, share-subscription agreements, board resolutions approving the capital injection, SWIFT MT103 payment evidence, tax references or tax returns, FATCA/CRS self-certifications, and an accountant's letter confirming the source of funds is consistent with the declared balance sheet.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Passive holding business with unclear downstream utilisation of cleared treasury funds
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: SPV business plan and holding rationale, subsidiary share-register entries, board minutes authorising future capital calls, dividend and funding forecasts, management-commercial agreements, transfer-pricing documentation if intercompany flows exist, and confirmation that no unauthorised third-party lending or opaque trust activity will pass through the account.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Sanctions, PEP, or adverse-media flags on the UBO or group
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Passport/biometric-residence proofs of all natural-person UBOs, independent sanctions-screening outputs from at least two commercial databases, non-PEP declarations, clean criminal-record certificates or confirmation of no adverse findings, shareholder declarations confirming no connections to designated persons, and, where any historical red flag exists, a detailed negative-media remediation narrative with contemporaneous explanatory documents.

cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.inbound_capital_injection_routing: Inbound equity subscription to the BVI holding SPV should be routed over SWIFT using MT103/MT202 for the base currency, with the remittance information field clearly stating 'EQUITY SUBSCRIPTION – SHARE CAPITAL CONTRIBUTION' and referencing the BVI entity name, shareholder name, and board-authorisation reference. For UK-disbursing bank accounts, the receiving bank will treat the credit as a capital-flow item and may request the source-of-funds pack described above; no UK exchange-control approval is required. Where the underlying investment is subsequently injected into a UK or EU operating subsidiary, the onward intercompany transfer should be made by MT103 with purpose reference 'LOAN OR EQUITY TO SUBSIDIARY', combined with a board resolution, loan agreement or subscription agreement, and transfer-pricing support. Use SWIFT GPI pre-verification to ensure same-day sender confirmation, and, for FX conversion, execute the conversion on the receiving bank's liquidity desk to maintain clear audit trails.
cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.outbound_trade_disbursements: Clearing rails should be selected according to currency and value: GBP high-value payments via CHAPS (Bank of England RTGS); GBP low-value and intra-group payments via Faster Payments; EUR payments via TARGET2 and SEPA Credit Transfer/Instant Credit Transfer; USD payments via SWIFT MT103 through UK bank correspondent accounts and the US Fedwire system. For trade finance, use confirmed irrevocable documentary letters of credit (SWIFT MT700/MT707) and documentary collections (MT400/MT422) when the BVI SPV finances subsidiary purchases from suppliers. All disbursements require corporate authority matrix signature validation, POD/invoice audit files, and bank screening to ensure harmonisation with UK AML obligations, BVI regulatory record-keeping, and any downstream sanctioned-entity prohibitions.
permissible_fx_hedging_instruments: Outright deliverable forward foreign exchange contracts against GBP, EUR, and USD, traded under standard ISDA/EMIR documentation and with collateral in an escrow or segregated margin account.

Non-deliverable forwards (NDFs) permissible only for hedging exposures in restricted, non-convertible, or less liquid underlying currencies where physical delivery is impeded; not required for GBP/USD/EUR but available on an exception basis through approved counterparty credit lines.

Cross-currency swaps and cross-currency interest-rate swaps permitted for long-term refinancing or dividend hedging, subject to UK EMIR clearing, margin, and reporting thresholds and board-approved treasury policy.

stage_6.form_identifier_and_portal: BVI Economic Substance Return (ESR) and BVI Annual Return filed through the BVI International Tax Authority and Registry of Corporate Affairs ROBO electronic portal
stage_6.statutory_deadline_rule: ESR filing due within 6 months after financial year end; corporate annual return due by 30 May for year ended 31 December, irrespective of tax result

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Legal name, BVI company number, financial year end, industry classification (ISIC 6420), registered agent details
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Declare as a BVI Business Company; no UK CT filing required unless UK central management and control or UK PE exists; indicate non-UK tax residence under DTR/domestic law

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Core income generating activities (CIGA) performed in BVI; number of directors, employees, physical offices; outsourcing arrangements; functions, assets, risks
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: For a pure equity holding SPV, declare 'reduced substance' status; no local employees required if outsourced authorized agent/registered agent; must maintain a registered office and at least one director

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Indicate management location, board minutes, bank accounts, and UK presence of directors/decisions
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: If board meetings and strategic decisions are in UK, note that UK HMRC may treat the BC as UK resident under s.14 CTA 2009; professional tax advice required; consider POEM exposure
